summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 2 in Infinitiv (JTM 1.1/90)

data.turoyo: <...> bəṯr mu nəfoso u ḥa, d huwele əḥtəyaǧ, xaṣṣatan meqəm, ʕuzliwole bi taššiye, saymiwole ḥuṭe bi taššiye bu taʕab dann iḏoṯo, an niše ʕuzliwole. <...>
data.translation: <...> Nach dem Auseinanderzupfen ... wer Bedarf hat ... vor allem früher, da spannen sie (die Wolle) auf der Spindel. In Handarbeit spannen sie sie auf der Spindel zu Fäden – die Frauen spannen sie. <...>

rationale: First Infinitiv example, an action nominal naming the same operation as the adjacent finite form; joint filing is provisional.

summary: New sense 2: tease, fluff out wool before spinning

data.gloss: tease, fluff out wool before spinning

rationale: The source orders washing, drying, kəmnafsile and then spinning; the following nəfoso names the same operation. This transitive wool-processing meaning differs from breathe. One passage with finite and nominal tokens; root identity remains provisional.

data.turoyo: <...> U ʕamrano d kmiqəṣ kmitaməlle geze. Kmaləfile w manṭən u ʕamro lu bayto, kmašəġile, bəṯr məd mašəġġe, kmanšəfile, bəṯr məd manšaffe, kəmnafsile, <...>
data.translation: <...> Die Wolle, die man schert, nennt man geze. Sie wickeln sie zusammen und bringen die Wolle nach Hause. Sie waschen sie, nach dem Waschen trocknen sie sie, und nachdem sie sie getrocknet haben, zupfen sie sie auseinander. <...>

rationale: First technical sense-2 finite example; preserves source n-f-s consonant order and the preparation sequence.

summary: The inherited breathe sense is intransitive, with b nḥiri expressing the bodily means. New kəmnafsile is transitive with wool as object (-le), and nəfoso is an action nominal in the same sequential description.

Permitted comparisons show nsf I zupfen with an editorial redirection to nṣf, nṣf I with different cited forms and senses, and nfṣ I shake/beat out. None establishes that the source's mnafs- should be silently respelled or moved. No nfš entry was found.
Both new tokens come from one passage and constitute one technical proposal, not two independent attestations. No unattested Preterit base form is supplied.

Does the source nfs textile verb belong to the same root as breathe, a homonymous nfs, a variant/metathesis related to nsf/nṣf, or an edition error for another root? The proposal preserves the printed order until checked.
Is nəfoso a regular II Infinitiv paired with mnafs- here? The action meaning is clear; its paradigm and the missing II citation forms need confirmation.
